name: McKenzie Pass · OR 242
description: 37 miles of Oregon Route 242 between Belknap Springs and Sisters, crossing McKenzie Pass through a 65-square-mile lava flow. Narrow and winding, with the Dee Wright Observatory at the summit and one of the longest seasonal closures of any road in this catalog.

sources.title: Travel Oregon: McKenzie Pass–Santiam Pass Scenic Byway

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Closed every year from November through mid-June due to snow — one of the longest closures of any road in this catalog, not a short winter gap. Check current status before a spring or fall trip specifically.

name: Historic Columbia River Highway · US 30 Historic
description: 24 miles of the original 1913–1922 Historic Columbia River Highway from Troutdale through the waterfall corridor — Latourell, Shepperd's Dell, Bridal Veil, Wahkeena and Multnomah Falls among them — toward Dodson. America's first planned scenic roadway, now a narrow two-lane road shared with heavy tourist and cyclist traffic.

sources.title: Oregon State Parks: Historic Columbia River Highway State Trail

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Multnomah Falls and other popular stops see real vehicle and pedestrian congestion, especially on weekends and in summer — a parking permit system is in effect at Multnomah Falls during peak season. This is a historic tourist road first, not a road to treat as a clear run.

name: Larch Mountain Road
description: 14 miles from the fork near Corbett to the Larch Mountain picnic area and trailhead, the highest road in Multnomah County's jurisdiction at 4,055 ft. Narrow in places with limited visibility, and heavily used by road cyclists.

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Closed every winter and spring, typically reopening in May and closing again in late November — exact dates depend on snow, not a fixed calendar.

name: Aufderheide Drive · FR 19
description: 58 miles of Forest Road 19 connecting Highway 58 at Westfir to Highway 126 at McKenzie Bridge, a National Scenic Byway through old-growth forest along the North Fork Willamette and McKenzie Rivers. Minimal traffic and, notably, no gas stations or cell service for the entire route.

sources.title: Travel Oregon: Aufderheide National Scenic Byway

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: No gas stations and no cell service anywhere along this route — fuel up and tell someone your plan before starting. A Forest Service road, not a state highway, so winter maintenance is not guaranteed the way it is on OR 242 or US 20.

name: Santiam Pass · US 20
description: 72 miles of US 20 between Sweet Home and Sisters, crossing Santiam Pass (4,817 ft) along the South Santiam River. Narrow and winding through Cascadia and the pass itself; corners tighten enough that carrying too much speed puts riders into the gravel shoulder.

sources.title: TripCheck: McKenzie Pass–Santiam Pass Scenic Byway

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Stays open year-round unlike McKenzie Pass nearby, but ice and sudden weather changes are real between October and March — check current conditions before a winter trip.

name: Dead Indian Memorial Road · CR 722
description: 36 miles between Ashland and the Cascade-Siskiyou area, one of the oldest trans-Cascade travel routes in southern Oregon, climbing through Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest toward the Upper Klamath Basin. Wide, open, sustained curves rather than tight technical work.

sources.title: Oregon Encyclopedia: Dead Indian Memorial Road
Motorcycle road review: Dead Indian Memorial Rd (Hwy 722)

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Climbs to roughly 5,000 ft, so winter ice and snow are real; check current Jackson County road conditions before a cold-season trip.

name: Highway 66 · Green Springs Highway
description: 60 miles of Oregon Route 66 between Ashland and Klamath Falls, leaving Ashland on tight rhythmic hairpins that gain 2,500 ft in a few miles before settling into a longer mountain crossing. Narrow shoulders and stingily placed guardrails above Tyler Creek Canyon.

sources.title: Pashnit: Highway 66 – Green Springs Highway, Oregon
Motorcycle Roads NorthWest: Oregon State Route 66 (Ashland to Klamath Falls)

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Check current ODOT conditions before a winter trip; the climb out of Ashland gains significant elevation quickly and sees real weather.

name: Hyatt Prairie Road
description: 10 miles connecting Highway 66 near Green Springs Inn to Dead Indian Memorial Road, past Hyatt Lake. Narrow, mostly single-lane in character and rougher pavement than either road it connects — but it turns the two into a genuine loop instead of an out-and-back.

speed.note: No reliable posted limit was found for this selected section. Follow current signs.

access.note: Narrower and rougher than the two roads it connects; treat it as a deliberate, slower link between them rather than a road to carry speed on.
